observation_summary: The verification process failed when an invocation on a different mock occurred within the same line as a verification call, causing the verification mode to be lost.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the control flow logic within the MockHandler. Previously, the code incorrectly discarded the verification mode if the mock being invoked did not match the mock associated with the verification mode. The fix introduces an 'else' block that correctly re-registers the verification mode via 'mockingProgress.verificationStarted(verificationMode)' when a mismatch occurs, ensuring the verification state is preserved for subsequent calls. This is a correction to the procedural logic of how verification modes are managed during invocation handling.
evidence_used: The fix modifies the control flow in MockHandler by adding an 'else' block.
The 'else' block calls 'mockingProgress.verificationStarted(verificationMode)' to re-add the verification mode when the mock being invoked does not match the verification mode's mock.
The bug report explicitly mentions the issue of verification failing when an extra call to a different mock is made in the same line.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves a conditional check, the core issue is the incorrect handling of the verification state (the algorithm for managing verification modes) rather than just a missing guard.
The fix is local to the MockHandler's invocation processing logic and does not involve correcting a structural association between two distinct objects or data structures.
